label: SQL
summary: Runs SQL queries through Sequelize against supported relational engines.

configuration.code: SQL query text using bind or replacement placeholders.
configuration.custom_data: Connection settings and optional query metadata.

connection_config.parse_bigint: PostgreSQL only, boolean, default false. pg returns int8/bigint as a string to avoid losing precision. Set true to receive a number for the values that fit in Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER; anything larger still arrives as a string, and numeric/decimal types are never converted.
connection_config.connection_override_allow: Optional array of dotted paths the request body is allowed to change via the runtime `connection` override, e.g. ["database", "options.host"]. Omitted by default, which means every key is overridable, including options.host, options.port, options.dialect and options.storage. Can only narrow, never widen: a body that declares its own value for this key is ignored. Every use of the override is logged to the server console with the paths that changed, never their values; it is not written to ofapi_log, which logs HTTP requests and feeds the traffic charts.
connection_config.options: REQUIRED. Sequelize options: dialect, host, port, ssl, dialectOptions, pool. The handler only opens a connection when both `options` and `code` are present, and it does not answer 400 when they are missing — the request just produces nothing useful. Note: if `custom_data` is empty, the handler silently falls back to the `$_VAR_SQLITE` AppVar, so a misconfigured endpoint can appear to work while reading a different database.
